key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and can be rapidly detected with imaging plus machine learning before severe failure occurs.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a fast, non-invasive pre-screening tool to flag unstable perovskite films, supporting scalable manufacturing of more reliable solar cells.
method: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy chemically identified harmful residual impurities.
High-resolution reflected light microscopy captured impurity patterns in as-prepared films.
Machine learning image analysis quantified impurity density for rapid stability screening.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation begins at impurity-perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded faster in early-stage tracking.
watch_item: The workflow appears to require careful calibration and chemical validation to avoid false positives when transferring to new film compositions or imaging setups.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
